title: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
summary: Unifies heterogeneous optical mocap collections through MoSh++ and a common parametric body surface representation.
limitations: Adjacent data infrastructure; a shared body representation does not itself supply compositional labels or object trajectories.

title: BABEL: Bodies, Action and Behavior with English Labels
summary: Adds sequence and temporally localized action language to AMASS, supporting action understanding and temporal composition.
limitations: Motion derives from AMASS; overlapping annotations do not establish unseen-combination generalization by themselves.

title: The KIT Motion-Language Dataset
summary: Aggregates mocap in a capture-independent representation with crowdsourced natural-language descriptions.
limitations: General motion-language resource; abstract does not specify a held-out compositional split.

title: Generating Diverse and Natural 3D Human Motions From Text
summary: Introduces HumanML3D and a stochastic text-to-motion baseline.
limitations: Learned embedding metrics measure statistical/text agreement; they do not certify contact mechanics or novel-combination execution.
method: Samples duration from text, then generates motion snippets with a temporal VAE.
conditions: Natural-language description; sampled or supplied length.
evaluation: HumanML3D and KIT-ML; FID, diversity, multimodality, R-precision and text-motion distance. R-precision ranks the paired caption against 31 distractors.

title: GRAB: A Dataset of Whole-Body Human Grasping of Objects
summary: Marker-based whole-body, articulated hand/face and object trajectories with detailed grasp interaction.
limitations: Source interactions are captured examples; dataset availability does not imply compositional holdout evaluation.

title: BEHAVE: Dataset and Method for Tracking Human Object Interactions
summary: Multi-view RGB-D body-object interaction data with body/object fits and contacts across everyday objects and locations.
limitations: Reconstruction and interaction resource, rather than a benchmark of unseen skill combinations.

title: InterCap: Joint Markerless 3D Tracking of Humans and Objects in Interaction
summary: Reconstructs whole-body SMPL-X and known objects from synchronized multi-view RGB-D, using contact cues.
limitations: Paper describes pseudo ground-truth fits; captured subjects/objects and sensor setting bound evidence.

title: HIMO: A New Benchmark for Full-Body Human Interacting with Multiple Objects
summary: Multi-object full-body mocap with text and temporal segments; diffusion branches and autoregressive segments support timeline control.
limitations: Abstract reports unseen geometry and temporal composition, but exact split leakage and metrics require full protocol review.

title: Motion-X: A Large-scale 3D Expressive Whole-body Human Motion Dataset
summary: Provides expressive SMPL-X motion, sequence semantic labels and frame-level descriptions from a scalable video annotation pipeline.
limitations: Automatically estimated motion/labels are not direct contact-force ground truth; not a dedicated compositional split.

title: COSMI: COmpositional Synthesis of Multi-object Interactions
summary: Composes contact-local captured interactions and learns a text-conditioned multi-object diffusion model.
limitations: Sustained interactions, rather than dependent multi-stage activities; prompt does not fix path/timing; finger precision remains limited.
method: Mirroring and body-part transfer, semantic/geometric compatibility checks; shared object slots and joint-relative object motion.
conditions: Caption, object geometry/name and initial poses.
evaluation: Holds out one chair instance and five interaction pairings; reports text-motion metrics, contacts, sliding, jerk, penetration and articulated motion. Composition split is not independent-subject evaluation.

title: SINC: Spatial Composition of 3D Human Motions for Simultaneous Action Generation
summary: Studies simultaneous actions through body-part motion composition and synthetic training examples.
limitations: Kinematic body-part combination is not evidence of physics-valid contact-rich manipulation.
method: GPT-guided action-to-body-part assignment selects relevant parts from two source motions and augments training.
evaluation: BABEL composition benchmark, baselines and text-supervised motion-encoder metric; ablates synthetic-data contribution.

title: Seamless Human Motion Composition with Blended Positional Encodings
summary: FlowMDM generates temporally composed text-conditioned motion and evaluates transition quality.
limitations: Independent low-frequency subsequence generation can limit relationships across actions; no contact-dynamics certification.
method: Blends absolute and relative positional encodings during diffusion with pose-centric cross-attention.
conditions: Sequence of text conditions and action durations.
evaluation: BABEL and HumanML3D; subsection/transition distribution metrics and jerk-based transition measures; compares TEACH and diffusion composition baselines.

title: Learning Generalizable Human Motion Generator with Reinforcement Learning
summary: Uses reinforcement learning and contrastive text-motion rewards on paired data and synthetic text-only prompts to improve generalization.
limitations: Semantic reward agreement does not establish physical execution; abstract-only protocol review.

title: SimDiff: Simulator-constrained Diffusion Model for Physically Plausible Motion Generation
summary: Conditions diffusion on environment coefficients and reports unseen combinations of environmental parameters.
limitations: Environmental-parameter composition differs from composing human action semantics; claims here follow the abstract.

title: DeepMimic: Example-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning of Physics-Based Character Skills
summary: Combines motion imitation and task objectives for simulated skills, recovery and multi-clip agents.
limitations: Simulated character control is adjacent to text-driven compositional generation; no claim of general unseen semantic combinations.

title: AMP: Adversarial Motion Priors for Stylized Physics-Based Character Control
summary: Learns motion-style rewards from unstructured clips alongside task rewards; reports emergent skill composition.
limitations: Task-reward-driven simulated control differs from one-shot text-conditioned generation and benchmarked semantic holdouts.

title: ASE: Large-Scale Reusable Adversarial Skill Embeddings for Physically Simulated Characters
summary: Learns reusable latent motor skills from unsegmented motion using adversarial imitation and unsupervised RL.
limitations: Downstream reward functions still specify tasks; reusable skills alone do not establish language-compositional generalization.

title: DiffMimic: Efficient Motion Mimicking with Differentiable Physics
summary: Uses differentiable physics for efficient reference motion imitation.
limitations: Motion tracking and training efficiency are adjacent capabilities; no compositional generation claim inferred.

title: Perpetual Humanoid Control for Real-time Simulated Avatars
summary: Scales physics-based imitation with recovery from falls and noisy reference motion.
limitations: Progressive training is costly; scene/terrain awareness and tighter upstream integration are future directions.
method: Progressive multiplicative control allocates capacity for difficult motions and recovery.
conditions: Reference pose sequence and simulated humanoid state.
evaluation: Large-scale mocap imitation, noisy video/language references and fail-state recovery timing; simulation avatar evidence.

title: Universal Humanoid Motion Representations for Physics-Based Control
summary: Distills a broad motion imitator into a variational latent representation with proprioception-conditioned prior for downstream hierarchical RL.
limitations: Original arXiv year 2023, ICLR 2024; simulator skill reuse is not an unseen language-combination benchmark.

title: MaskedMimic: Unified Physics-Based Character Control Through Masked Motion Inpainting
summary: Unifies masked keyframes, objects, text and mixed descriptions as partial motion constraints for simulated character control.
limitations: Composing input modalities and task transitions is different from proving arbitrary unseen action combinations.

title: CLoSD: Closing the Loop between Simulation and Diffusion for multi-task character control
summary: Closes a feedback loop between an autoregressive text/target-conditioned diffusion planner and an RL tracker for task sequences.
limitations: Original arXiv 2024, ICLR 2025; demonstrated task suite does not imply arbitrary long-horizon generalization.

title: Expressive Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Robots
summary: Tracks upper-body expression while lower-body velocity control enables robust locomotion, with real robot demonstrations.
limitations: Leg imitation is relaxed; expressive locomotion does not establish dexterous object-task composition.

title: Learning Multi-Modal Whole-Body Control for Real-World Humanoid Robots
summary: Masked-motion curriculum learns multimodal control and combines joystick locomotion with partial-body mimicry.
limitations: Control-modality combination is adjacent to semantic compositional generation; abstract-level review.

title: BeyondMimic: From Motion Tracking to Versatile Humanoid Control via Guided Diffusion
summary: Combines robust motion tracking with a distilled diffusion policy and test-time cost guidance for navigation and control.
limitations: Real hardware evidence is task-specific; does not establish arbitrary object manipulation or semantic composition.

title: Retargeting Matters: General Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Motion Tracking
summary: Studies how retargeting quality affects BeyondMimic tracking on LAFAN1 and introduces GMR.
limitations: Retargeting fidelity and tracking robustness are prerequisites, not compositional generation results.

title: MoCapAct: A Multi-Task Dataset for Simulated Humanoid Control
summary: Provides a multi-task resource for simulated humanoid control and reusable motion-capture skills.
limitations: Simulated control data; not a human-object composition dataset or real robot execution corpus.

title: MaskAdapt: Learning Flexible Motion Adaptation via Mask-Invariant Prior for Physics-Based Characters
summary: Mask-invariant base policy plus residual adaptation enables multi-part composition and text-driven partial tracking.
limitations: Targeted body-part adaptation in simulation is not full contact-rich compositional generalization.

title: Weave: Learning Whole-Body Dexterous Loco-Manipulation from Human-Object Interactions
summary: Contact-aware retargeting and approach completion feed a geometry/contact-aware whole-body and finger controller; releases simulated robot-object rollouts.
limitations: Parallel simulation rollouts are not hardware recordings; training/unseen sequence success is not arbitrary object or task generalization.
method: Constructs executable interaction references, then tracks them with coordinated body and finger control.
conditions: Robot/object state, geometric and reference interaction information.
evaluation: Nine-object simulation suite, trained and held-out sequences plus architecture/optimizer ablations. Approximately 9,000 rollouts/23 hours are simulated execution.

title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation
summary: Retargets heterogeneous HOI, learns a generalist simulation tracker and iteratively retains task-preserving perturbations that execute successfully.
limitations: Augmented executable corpus is simulation-generated; abstract also reports robot transfer, whose task scope requires full-paper review.

title: GRAIL: Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models
summary: Grounds generated videos in known 3D scenes/assets, recovers HOI, retargets and trains trackers and visual policies.
limitations: Uses privileged known configurations; generated data is virtual. Real G1 deployment results are separate task-specific policy evidence.

title: RoboMoCap: A Large-Scale Whole-Body Motion Capture Dataset with Egocentric Vision for Robot Learning
summary: Pairs egocentric/wrist observations with optical whole-body capture for locomotion, transport and manipulation; benchmarks reconstruction, foot estimation and retargeting.
limitations: Captured human demonstrations and retargeting benchmarks do not establish learned compositional robot policy success.

title: HiPHI: A Large-Scale Benchmark for High-Precision Human Motion and Object-Interaction
summary: Optical whole-body motion and mesh-level object trajectories organized for broad primitive coverage; evaluates diversity, grounding and consistency.
limitations: Dataset coverage is not a compositional held-out policy result; marker accuracy should not be equated with all reconstructed body/contact accuracy.
